summary: The counting explanation and prevalence comparison are well supported, but the decisive spoken answer incorrectly equates 9/108 with 90% and contradicts the planned visual result.

issues.detail: The Reveal says 'Nine out of a hundred eight: ninety percent.' Recalculation gives 9/108=1/12, approximately 8.3%, not 90%. This is the central answer and contradicts both the displayed fraction/result and the following distinction between sensitivity and the probability after a positive. Correct the spoken percentage to approximately 8.3% and keep narration and visuals aligned; retain 90% only for the different denominator, 9/10.

checks: The supplied counts give sensitivity 9/10=90%, false-positive rate 99/990=10%, 108 total positives and positive-conditioned share 9/108 approximately 8.3%.
The second hypothetical population correctly yields 90 positives from 100 with the condition and 90 from 900 without it, hence 90/180=50% with both test rates fixed.

Regrouping preserves original membership colors and positive outlines, visibly explaining why the denominator changes; the second population is explicitly substituted rather than depicting original people becoming ill.
The six-second pause follows a bounded spoken invitation with sufficient known counts, and the plan withholds the answer until Reveal.
Exactly three classic scenes and the explicit toy-example caveat match the request; the narrated default needs no interaction.

363 spoken words plus six seconds of silence estimate approximately 166-198 seconds at 125-150 words per minute with the supplied 10% allowance, consistent with roughly three minutes; no measured audio was supplied.
